xenonet net [create|join|status|hosts|add-machine|remove|leave|set|approve|gateway]

One XenoNet network across your machines. One machine is the network's
gateway; the others link to it over HTTP(S), so no machine opens a port
and nothing needs SSH keys. Frames between machines are signed by the one
that sent them and sealed for the one they're for: the gateway passes them
on and can't read them.

  xenonet net create --name <name> --host <id> [--lan <ip:port>]
                                   makes a network, with this machine as its
                                   founder and gateway. Other machines reach
                                   the gateway through the actor gateway's
                                   tunnel (xenonet gateway on --tunnel …), or
                                   on your LAN at --lan, an address this
                                   machine has (never 0.0.0.0)
  xenonet net join <address> <ticket>
                                   joins the network, with the line Add a
                                   machine showed: it works once, for ten
                                   minutes. A ticket made on a machine that
                                   isn't the gateway waits for that machine
                                   to sign this one in
  xenonet net status [--json]      the network, this machine, the gateway and
                                   the link, and what waits to be sent
  xenonet net hosts [--json]       the machines in the network
  xenonet net add-machine <id> [--window]
                                   a ticket for a new machine, and the line to
                                   run there. --window when you'll use a
                                   XenoNet window on it. It's XenoNet's
                                   window's (Add a machine), since signing
                                   the machine in asks you
  xenonet net remove <id>          takes a machine out of the network
  xenonet net revoke-device        revoking a lost machine's device is
                                   XenoNet's window's (Network settings ›
                                   Your devices), since it asks you
  xenonet net replace <id>         takes a reinstalled machine's old keys out,
                                   and makes a ticket for it to join again
  xenonet net leave [--force]      asks to be taken out, then forgets the
                                   network here; this XenoNet carries on alone
  xenonet net set [--titles-only | --no-titles-only]
                  [--share-load | --no-share-load] [--lan <ip:port>]
                  [--start off|you|network|delegate] [--wake consent|network]
                                   what this machine shares with the network
                                   (its load: CPU, GPU, memory and the parts,
                                   on by default), a LAN-only gateway's
                                   address, who may start sessions here (you,
                                   by default; network adds the network's
                                   sessions and actors; delegate is the
                                   network, with what they start running
                                   under your delegation) and who may wake
                                   them for a message (your consent per
                                   session, by default, or the network).
                                   Start and wake are entries in the
                                   network's chain: narrowing is done at
                                   once, and widening asks you, so it's done
                                   from XenoNet's window. Your delegation is
                                   an entry in your own chain, signed by
                                   your device: it names your devices (all
                                   of them, unless you narrow it), lets
                                   them start sessions and allow routine
                                   prompts inside the session's folder for
                                   work you started on any of them, and
                                   lasts a year. Setting delegate makes it
                                   when none names the machine's device,
                                   which asks you once more
  xenonet net set --on <id> [--start …] [--wake …] [--approve <id>]
                                   another machine's start and wake, from a
                                   window host. Narrowing is done at once;
                                   network and delegate ask you, so they're
                                   set from XenoNet's window, and take the
                                   founder, or wait for another window host
                                   to --approve it there. Delegate needs the
                                   machine to have a device of yours, which
                                   your delegation names
  xenonet net gateway take [--lan <ip:port>]
                                   makes this machine the network's gateway,
                                   at that LAN address or through the actor
                                   gateway's tunnel. On the founder's machine
                                   it's done; elsewhere it waits for the
                                   founder or another window host to approve
  xenonet net approve <id> [--op <op>]
                                   approves what waits for approval about a
                                   machine, such as its move to gateway or
                                   its add as a window host, and shows what
                                   it approves. Several waiting: name one by
                                   the entry id the answer lists
  xenonet net gateway set <address>
                                   follows the gateway to a new address, when
                                   this machine missed the move

Creating, joining and leaving are yours to do: XenoNet refuses them from
under an agent. The founder's key is the network's root: a network whose
founder is lost is made again.
